name: X-linked Complex Spastic Paraplegia

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for X-linked Complex Spastic Paraplegia

criteria.description: Progressive lower limb spasticity and weakness
Family history consistent with X-linked inheritance pattern
Presence of additional neurological symptoms such as ataxia, cognitive impairment, or peripheral neuropathy
Identification of pathogenic mutation in known X-linked spastic paraplegia gene
Exclusion of other causes of spastic paraplegia by neuroimaging and metabolic testing

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Progressive lower limb spasticity with X-linked family history and presence of complex neurological features; genetic confirmation supports diagnosis.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing is recommended for confirmation but diagnosis can be made clinically in presence of characteristic features and family history.

searchTerms: tightness and muscle spasms in legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: X-linked pattern of inheritance evident in family history

searchTerms: complex neurological symptoms including uncoordinated movement
brain and nerve involvement with balance issues
difficulty walking due to leg weakness

common.symptomName: Cognitive impairment ranging from mild to moderate
Bladder dysfunction including urgency and incontinence

laboratory: Exclusion of metabolic causes of spastic paraplegia
imaging: MRI brain and spinal cord may show corticospinal tract degeneration
genetic: Pathogenic variants in X-linked spastic paraplegia genes (e.g., SPG genes located on X chromosome)
other: Nerve conduction studies abnormal in some cases

distinguishingFeatures: Usually pure spastic paraplegia without complex neurological features
Lack of prominent spasticity in early stages

redFlags: Rapid progression of spasticity and weakness
Presence of systemic symptoms such as fever or weight loss
references: Orphanet: X-linked Complex Spastic Paraplegia - ORPHA:98888
